newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol to study sites for second Dutch airport.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol to study sites for second Dutch airport.

text.p: Amsterdam airport's operating company has started a study into three alternative sites for a second Dutch national airport, company spokeswoman Marianne de Bie told Reuters on Thursday.
She added that the study has been launched to be ready for a wide public debate on the subject, expected to begin next February or March.
All three options would involve extensive land reclamation or the construction of artificial island, she said.

One option would be to build an island in the North Sea; another would be to reclaim land from the inner reaches of the Ijsselmeer, a large, man-made expanse of water near Amsterdam; the third option involves building an airport near the entrance to the port of Rotterdam, on a proposed land reclamation site called the Tweede Maasvlakte.
De Bie said the airport operating company is not at this stage backing any one of the options at the expense of the other two.
She added: "We are preparing ourselves for the debate that will come next year when the Dutch parliament completes its first report on the entire subject of a second national airport."
At the same time the airport's management does not intend to back suggestions from Dutch environmental groups to move Schiphol itself to a new, offshore location, he said.
"We think that the location of Schiphol as a multi-modal hub for the future, in which billions of guilders have already been invested, is here and it is here to stay," De Bie added.
